The 9/14 working day closes here. Nine phases opened and closed in one session (P0-P4, P7 cells 1-4, the GitHub MTP-acceptance recon), three motivated-closure decisions (D18 general CPU route, D19 cache-hit gap, D24 prefetch) and one acquired asset (D26). The next session resumes from HANDOFF_14_SETTEMBRE.md, which collects the full map of tracks, the bench reference numbers, the knobs introduced today, and the method rules learned today.

P7 cell 5: opening A7 CLOSED (9/15, commit 7e16b85). The CPU contribution on MTP draft rows never reached moe_out: it was exactly zero. Root cause: the export kernel writes the job descriptor with a fixed row stride (row * MOE_CPU_MAX_PER_ROW + e), the pool read it with a compacted cursor -- the two addressing schemes coincide only when every route sits on row 0, which is the case for all of P3, all of P4, and P2's host bench (540,672 float comparisons at zero differences that could not see the defect for that reason). On draft rows the pool read cells the export kernel zeroes at the start of every job -- expert 0, weight 0.0 -- both of which pass every domain and finiteness check, so the pool ran the full arithmetic and multiplied it by zero. Fixed together with two collateral defects: a slot admitted in diagnostic mode for a draft-only miss was left with no recency (last_used=0), which trapped the planner (__trap()) on the next call; the draft-only flag kept polluting the cache policy even in diagnostic mode. Verification: draft-row NRMSE 1.000000 -> 0.012958, acceptance 0.69652 -> 0.79298 (above the 0.76990 lane-off reference), lane-off fingerprints identical to M1. All three fixes are adopted: two are genuine correctness defects (one lethal), the third is a zero-cost safety net; P3/P4 results remain valid because every one of their runs was single-row, where the two addressing schemes coincide by construction.

P7 cell 5: the CPU lane on MTP draft rows is NEGATIVE at 2 threads. The R < 13 ms gate is missed: R = 22.20 ms (worse than cell 4's 19.7 ms, but honestly so -- that number came from a pool multiplying expert 0 by zero 155 times with perfect cache locality, this one is real arithmetic on 155 different experts). t/s 28.086 vs 30.827 on the same binary, -8.9%. Decomposition: delivery alone is -4.29 ms/cycle (R = 11.48, would clear the gate by itself), CPU arithmetic is +11.17 ms/cycle (155 experts x 72 us/expert, a third independent confirmation of the 9/10 number); the missing factor is 2.6. Minimum free RAM 7.08 GB. One more test before final closure: cell 6, LLAMA_MOE_CPU_THREADS at 4 and 6 with pool affinity -- if the cycle does not drop below T5's 57.41 ms even at 6 threads, the lane closes for good. New binding method rule: a host bench that only exercises row 0 does not validate a multi-row descriptor -- every future executor test must include routes on rows > 0.

P7 cell 6 (9/15, commit 6e7f879): the CPU lane on MTP draft rows is CLOSED FOR GOOD. Test A3' swept LLAMA_MOE_CPU_THREADS at 3/4/6 with auto affinity against T5 (lane off, cycle 57.41 ms) and T6 (2 threads, 63.84 ms). No configuration drops below the off-lane cycle: the minimum is at 4 threads, cycle 61.15 ms (+3.74 ms vs T5, R = 19.51 ms against the 13 ms gate, tps 29.319); 3 threads is 64.82 ms (R = 23.17) and 6 threads is 65.59 ms (R = 23.94), both worse than 2 threads. The curve is non-monotonic -- 4 clearly beats 2 (-12.1% on R, +4.4% on tps) but 3 and 6 are both worse than 2, falsifying cell 5's linear-scaling hypothesis (that 6 threads would flip the sign). Per-expert CPU cost drops to ~52 us only at 4 threads (vs the 72-76 us reference band; 69/75/80 us at 2/3/6). Arithmetic (routes, -46.61% bytes, zero non-finite) is identical across all thread counts, verified via counters, not assumed. Single replica per configuration, declared limit.

The speculation track is EXHAUSTED within the current architecture (P7 cell 6, 9/15). With the CPU lane closed (D31), only minor, unquantified, lossless levers remain on the verify row: A6a (QSA bias in F16/on-device instead of host H2D, +1.14 ms today), A6b (dedup the QSA gather across the two verify rows, k_get_rows headroom at 3.7 GiB/s, not quantified), A2 (the polling plumbing from D26 applied to the P4 extension, 41.9 us/active layer measured but not benched on the free set). None of the three, nor their sum, is measured on free-form decode; an honest, unmeasured estimate (HANDOFF_14_SETTEMBRE.md section 3.6) puts them together at +3-5% at most above the 28.66 t/s reference -- none reaches the 50 t/s goal. P7 moves from IN PROGRESS to SUSPENDED: no cell remains open without a structural decision from the user (see HANDOFF_14_SETTEMBRE.md section 3.6 for the five structural options, listed without a recommendation).

Token budget 2048 for quality runs with reasoning off at long context, 9/15. At 131k with --reasoning off and budget 1024, both free-form cases in cell 7 produce solid but truncated text (4 of 5 rubric criteria met each) -- reasoning is empty but the final prose at long context needs more than the screening budget. Budget is a bench max_tokens parameter, not a model property; D11 remains the reference for speed screening.

Lever B (device-resident QSA bias) is adopted; A, C, D1 are not (P8, COMPLETE 9/15, commit cc91ebb). Of four lossless levers measured cumulatively at the 131k operating point, only B is distinguishable from noise: -1.44 ms on R (5 runs vs 4, groups separated by over six standard deviations), +2.3% on t/s. With B, MTP draft-1 flips from a net loss (-0.5% vs off, raw R1) to a gain (+1.8%, 26.87 vs 26.38 t/s). A is redundant once B is on; C buys nothing (the project's occupancy hypothesis is falsified); D1 shortens the graph by 84 nodes but does not save time (pays in locality), shipped off by default. The delivered patch (p8_cumulativa.patch) defaults to A off (redundant), B on, C on (free and bit-identical), D1 off. The 2-token draft stays closed even with every lever (-11.2% vs draft-1); the only large remaining lever is the P4/P5 CPU lane on the 6.5 ms of expert gather, which P8 does not touch by design. Side effect: the GGUF contains not a single IQ3_XXS tensor (all 144 expert tensors are IQ2_S/IQ3_S/IQ4_NL) -- lever E of the CPU/GPU project must be redesigned against mmvq.cu's scalar branch, not mul_mat_vec_q_moe.

50 tps at 131k does NOT fit on this hardware with this model (P9, COMPLETE 9/15, commit 4cfa390). The byte floor at 131k -- 5.11 GiB/token at measured bandwidths (VRAM 340.3 GB/s, PCIe 26.3 GB/s) -- is 21.9 ms with today's lane overlap (24.208 ms without overlap); 50 tps is 20.0 ms/token, which sits BELOW that floor before paying a single kernel launch, a single dequantization, a single idle gap. Today's 37.44 ms token (nsys, 106 forwards, geometric integrity check, 4/4 fingerprints identical to P8 R0): dense matvec 15.69 ms/41.9% (Q6_K 9.609 ms, ~82% of peak bandwidth), PCIe expert transport 6.688 ms/17.9% (bus-saturated, 100%), VRAM expert matvec 5.929 ms/15.8% (IQ2_S 3.985 at 36.4% of peak), QSA indexer 3.206 ms/8.6%, GPU idle 3.322 ms/8.9% (two-thirds in two ~1ms gaps per forward, always at the same phase between the graph and the host), elementary ops 2.512 ms/6.7% over 1,956 launches, rest 2.404 ms, kernel overlap -2.310 ms. Three facts: (1) at the operating point the largest single item is dense Q6_K, not expert upload (the reverse at short context); (2) single-row matvec is weight-bound, not byte-bound -- IQ2_S costs 1.606 ps/weight of pure dequantization vs 0.398 for Q6_K (4x), so at one row 2.5 bits/weight cost as much as 6.87 effective bpw; (3) inverting transport time to measured bandwidth yields 168.5 MiB, 1.86 missing experts/layer, 81.4% implicit hit rate, which does NOT match P7's direct device counters at 205k (70.5%) -- unreconciled, does not change the verdict. Three identified levers with expected ms: Q6_K->Q4_K -1.6..-2.6 ms (NOT lossless, changes weights, real quality risk, frees 841 MiB VRAM); fusing hc_ connection launches -1.0..-1.9 ms (lossless to be proven, high difficulty); IQ2_S kernel -1.4..-1.9 ms (lossless by construction). Verdict table: today 37.91 ms = 26.4 tps; lossless levers only ~34.3 ms = 29.1 tps; all three levers ~32.4 ms = 30.8 tps; + idle GPU cut to 1 ms ~30.1 ms = 33.2 tps; most optimistic imaginable ~28 ms = ~36 tps; physical byte floor (fiction) 21.9 ms = 45.7 tps. Honest single-token target: 30-33 tps.

P10 cell 2 COMPLETE (9/15, commit 9b597eb): the two GPU-idle gaps between the CUDA graph and the host are of different kinds. Gap 1 (1.267 ms/forward, once per token) is the boundary between one forward and the next (graph node 0, between the output head mul_mat_vec_q<q6_k> of graph N and the first node of graph N+1): sampling/serving + set_inputs (0.505 ms host, no CUDA calls), 15 input copies with 42 syncs (0.271 ms), an 8,191-node CUDA-graph compatibility rescan (0.174 ms), graph launch. Gap 2 (0.080 ms) is inside the replay at node 45 -- only a cudaGraphLaunch still being delivered by the driver (~0.75 us/node), not fixable by this cell's levers. Per-forward cudaStreamSynchronize calls were 43.61, not 78 (P8's lever B had already removed ~34): 1 necessary, 15.59 blocking copy-queue waits, 27.02 pre-input queue drains -- 42.6 of 43.6 were convenience waits, caused by input copies running on cudaStreamPerThread instead of the graph's own stream. Two lossless levers behind a default-on switch fixed this: GGML_SCHED_ASYNC_INPUTS (split inputs copied with set_tensor_async on the graph's stream, one sync per split instead of two per input: copy block 271 -> 133 us, syncs 43.61 -> 9.12) and GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_COMPAT_CACHE (the graph-compatibility verdict cached by uid instead of rescanning 8,191 nodes every forward: 174 -> 5 us). Side finding: the 2 splits at bs=1 are one CUDA and one CPU (-ot per_layer_token_embd.weight=CPU keeps 26.8 GiB in a host buffer). Measured at the bench: V2 = 37.332 ms/token (mean of two replicas, 37.408/37.256) = 26.786 tps vs V1 37.486 ms/token = 26.677 tps, i.e. only -0.154 ms/token -- below the -0.5 ms/token adoption gate by roughly a factor of three, because most of the boundary gap was host work (0.852 of 1.267 ms), 0.505 ms of it untouched by this cell, and a quarter of what is removed at the boundary reappears inside gap 2 (0.080 -> 0.138 ms). Fingerprints identical 16/16 across all four runs. First direct measurement of replica noise on T1 at 131k: 0.152 ms on the aggregate (not the 0.5 ms assumed so far, which comes from P8's verify-row R). Decision: the patch stays on as path hygiene (costs nothing: no extra node, byte, VRAM, or text risk) but is NOT counted as an adopted lever, and does not move P9's ceiling (D37). Updated noise rule: the 131k adoption gate stays at -0.5 ms/token because it is roughly three times the measured noise, not because the noise itself was 0.5. Remaining targets: the 505 us of unresolved host work inside the boundary gap, and the 5-20 us band inside the graph (0.885 ms/token, larger than the boundary gap after this cell, still unexplained). P10 cell 3 COMPLETE (9/15, commit 51ff69c): the single-row IQ2_S expert MMVQ kernel is adopted at occupancy level 1. Root cause was occupancy, not the code-table lookup P9 had guessed: the real instance (ncols_dst=1, gate+up fusion, small_k) uses 110 registers/thread and lives at 4 blocks/SM of 12 possible (33%). All three 'obvious' ideas from P9 are bit-identical in the microbench and all slower -- code table in shared memory +3.0%, q8_1 activations in shared memory +7.1%, weights read with .cg outside L1 +23.6% (L1 was earning its keep). Fix is a one-line change: the mul_mat_vec_q template takes an int min_blocks=1 that feeds __launch_bounds__'s second argument; the dispatcher sets it to 8 only on the single-row + small_k path for table-quantized types (iq2_s at level 1, iq4_nl also at level 2, GGML_CUDA_MMVQ_OCCUPANCY switch, default on for iq2_s only). ptxas drops to 64 registers with zero spills, blocks/SM 4->8; verified lossless twice (microbench memcmp against all 6,400 output floats on real iq2_s weights, and 4/4 fingerprints identical at the bench across two replicas). In situ: kernel 82.88 -> 66.21 us/launch (-20.1%), bandwidth 126.6 -> 158.5 GB/s, efficiency against the byte floor 36.4% -> 46.6%; no other quant type moves (q6_k unchanged to the nanosecond over 27,595 launches). At the bench: V2 37.332 -> V3 36.703 ms/token = 26.786 -> 27.245 tps (mean of two replicas each), -0.629 ms/token (+1.71%), against a V3 replica-to-replica noise of 0.068 ms -- the -0.5 ms adoption gate is cleared by nine times that noise. IQ4_NL (level 2) measured neutral (36.760 ms/token, inside the V3 replica spread) and NOT adopted, switch left off. Cumulative lossless candidate at the 131k operating point: R0 26.381 -> B (D39) 26.677 -> boundary-gap hygiene (D40) 26.786 -> occupancy (D41) 27.245 tps, +3.3% over R0, identical text throughout. Two open, non-lossless leads remain on this kernel: 48 of 128 threads per block never execute a vec_dot (blocks_per_row_x=10 vs blocks_per_iter=16, warp 3 entirely dead -- real utilization is only 41.7% of the max even at 8 blocks/SM; recovering them changes reduction order, not bit-identical), and 1.05 ms/token still sits above the byte floor (table lookup + sign arithmetic). P10 now has no open cell: it awaits a user decision among four choices -- (a) dense Q6_K->Q4_K residents (-1.6..-2.6 ms + 841 MiB VRAM freed, NOT lossless, needs quality rubrics first); (b) recovering the 48 dead threads (largest remaining kernel lever, not bit-identical); (c) the 505 us of unresolved host time at the forward boundary (cell 2, needs NVTX); (d) P6 quality/stability validation of the cumulative lossless candidate (quality rubrics, 30-minute stability, rollback plan) for promotion to bin_prod.
